criteria.text: A user can initialize a valid Git worktree without starting a task.
A user can start one task from a preset or custom procedure.
`status` makes the active stage, attempt, item state, blockers, and pending jobs clear.
`next` lists every missing required item and a structured command suggestion.
A stage cannot complete with missing required items, changed required local artifacts, or open blockers.
The common interface emphasizes current task execution rather than historical evidence.
Custom ordered procedures validate and run without source changes.
Procedure snapshots are immutable for a running session.
All six item types and constraints behave as specified.
Skip works only when explicitly permitted.
A running session has exactly one active attempt.
Retry creates a clean attempt of the same stage.
Return creates a clean destination attempt and marks reached downstream stages `redo`.
Reopen applies the same redo semantics to a completed session.
Cancelled sessions cannot reopen.
Reset removes the task session and its session-local history.
`podwayd` is the sole normal writer.
Mutations are durable before admission acknowledgement.
FIFO ordering is proven within one worktree.
independent worktrees can execute mutations concurrently.
same-item concurrent updates cannot silently overwrite.
cursor commands cannot apply to a different active stage.
client retry after lost response does not duplicate a mutation.
queued jobs survive daemon restart while the worktree remains discoverable.
job cancellation works only before claim.
Every defined crash-injection point has a deterministic valid recovery outcome.
A state transition and terminal job result commit atomically.
A failed job changes no session state.
Running jobs recover to queued after daemon restart when no terminal commit exists.
Reset-all recovers idempotently from an interrupted marker state.
Workspace commands fail outside a valid non-bare Git worktree.
Main and linked worktrees are supported.
Path and symlink escapes are rejected.
Copied live workspace UUID conflicts are detected.
A moved worktree can repair its registry path after identity validation.
Runtime state remains inside `.podway/runtime/` and is ignored by Git.
Deleting the worktree deletes task state and queued jobs.
SQLite schema, foreign keys, WAL, and synchronous durability are configured as specified.
Migration diagnostics identify predecessor `schema-0-uninitialized` and result `schema-v1` for the non-file `uninitialized-database` initialization fixture.
Deterministic schema-0 to v1 conformance proves required pragmas, transactional initialization, no user task-state loss, no duplicated mutation, and no partial installation.
Migrations are transactional and checksummed.
Unsupported newer state fails closed.
Corrupt state fails closed and is diagnosable.
Destructive reset-all recreates a usable workspace.
Terminal jobs, idempotency data, and journal remain bounded according to policy.
No global task-state copy exists.
Every public command has complete help.
Every public command emits valid versioned JSON.
Public error codes and exit codes match the catalog.
Text and JSON never disagree on successful state.
zsh, bash, and fish completion are shipped and tested.
IPC rejects unsupported versions and oversized or malformed frames safely.
Automation can pass explicit revision, attempt, item revision, and idempotency values.
Both `podway` and `podwayd` install and run natively on the sole supported tuple `{triple: aarch64-apple-darwin, arch: arm64, host_arch: arm64, mach_o_arch: arm64}`.
LaunchAgent install is idempotent.
Daemon starts at user login.
Explicit stop, start, restart, status, logs, and uninstall work.
Socket and runtime permissions are correct.
Stale sockets and unexpected daemon exits recover.
Service uninstall preserves all worktree state.
No command executes arbitrary procedure-defined code.
No command performs Git mutation.
No daemon component listens on a network socket or performs network I/O.
Artifact bytes are never stored.
Logs exclude item values and task content by default.
Same-user trust limitations are documented in help and release documentation.
No workspace access key or misleading authentication claim exists.
`sw-dev`, `bug-fix`, `docs-only`, and `analysis` validate against the shipped schema.
Each preset has clear help and stage descriptions.
Each preset passes a complete end-to-end scenario.
Each preset passes at least one retry and one return scenario across the conformance suite.
Rust lockfile is committed.
Apple Silicon (`aarch64-apple-darwin`) binaries are built and exercised on the local arm64 release host.
Release archive contains both binaries, completions, schemas, presets, README, and MIT License.
Public artifacts have documented signing and notarization status.
Upgrade from the previous supported database schema is tested.
Release notes document contract versions and any migration.
Procedure starts enforce digest guards, durable admitted snapshots, source-drift and restart independence, digest-bound idempotent replay, and consistent returned Procedure identity.
Mutation response loss reconciles by idempotency key without duplicate admission or cancellation, across pre-admission disconnect, wait timeout, every job state, domain failure, and terminal pruning.

obligations.statement: Completion rejects when any required item is unsatisfied.
Completion rejects when required local-artifact evidence no longer matches the current artifact.
Completion rejects while the active attempt has an open blocker.
Every rejected completion preserves the prior aggregate and revision.
A stage whose policy explicitly permits skip can be skipped.
A stage without explicit skip permission rejects skip.
A rejected skip preserves the prior aggregate and revision.
Every normal public mutation route enters framed daemon IPC.
The daemon runtime opens and executes the writable workspace store lifecycle.
A closed-world crate, dependency, and public-API inventory exposes no normal non-daemon workspace-state writer.
A successful admission acknowledgement is returned only after the admission transaction commits.
An independent reopen replays the exact acknowledged idempotency receipt.
An independent reopen observes the admitted mutation in durable queue state.
The mutation transmits the caller-selected active-attempt cursor precondition.
Authoritative active-stage drift rejects the cursor mutation.
Drift neither retargets the request to the new cursor nor changes session state.
Queued jobs persist across daemon-equivalent store close and reopen.
Reopen resolves the same worktree identity and can enumerate its jobs.
Persisted queued jobs remain claimable in workspace FIFO order.
The executed registry exactly equals every controller-defined crash-injection point, with no omissions or extras.
Every registered point is exercised by a bound crash scenario.
Every crash scenario observes forced child-process termination at its point.
Reopen at every point produces its declared deterministic valid recovery outcome.
A successful state transition and terminal job result become durable in one commit.
A terminal pre-commit failure leaves the state transition unapplied.
A terminal pre-commit failure leaves no terminal job result.
Reopen after commit observes both the transition and terminal result.
Every reset-all marker/publication interruption boundary is exercised.
Recovery yields only a complete prior state or complete replacement state.
Retrying the same reset-all identity converges without duplicate mutation.
Recovery removes Store-owned interrupted marker/publication temporary state.
Runtime state is created only below `.podway/runtime/`.
The workspace-local Git ignore bytes exactly ignore `runtime/`.
Initialization replay neither broadens nor duplicates the ignore rule.
The deleted-worktree scenario first persists task state and at least one queued job.
Deleting the worktree removes its workspace-local SQLite state and side files.
Recovery classifies the registered identity as worktree-gone and does not adopt a copy.
The deleted task state and queued job cannot be enumerated or executed after recovery.
Conformance starts from the exact schema-0-uninitialized predecessor and verifies the required schema-v1 pragmas and objects.
An injected initialization failure rolls back to schema 0 with no partial v1 installation.
All state admitted in the schema-0 fixture is preserved except the explicitly declared v1 installation changes.
Reopen records one migration and does not duplicate task state or a user mutation.
Migration failure rolls back the whole migration transaction.
The failed migration leaves the predecessor structurally schema 0.
Successful migration records the exact approved v1 migration checksum.
A tampered or missing migration checksum fails closed.
Public reset-all removes seeded session-local task history.
Reset-all recreates a valid schema and workspace identity.
A fresh session start and mutation succeed in the recreated workspace.
Replaying the acknowledged reset-all identity does not reset or mutate again.
Terminal jobs obey the frozen minimum, age, and maximum retention policy.
Idempotency records obey their scope-specific retention policy and retained terminal receipts still replay exactly after job pruning.
Operational journal rows obey the frozen age, minimum-newest, and maximum-row policy.
Successful mutation or idle maintenance invokes pruning without allowing unbounded growth.
The proof enumerates the complete frozen public-command set, not a sample.
Every public command success emits one valid versioned JSON envelope.
Every JSON envelope identifies the invoked route and its typed result.
Every exercised public-command failure emits a valid versioned JSON error envelope.
Text and JSON modes execute the same successful status scenario.
Active stage, attempt, item state, blockers, and pending-job semantics project equally in both modes.
Both modes send the identical typed daemon request contract.
An explicit session revision reaches the exact protocol precondition field.
An explicit attempt ID reaches the exact protocol precondition field.
An explicit item revision reaches the exact protocol precondition field.
An explicit idempotency key reaches the exact protocol field unchanged.
Representative public workspace mutations preserve complete Git administrative metadata bytes.
A closed-world public-API inventory exposes no Git mutation operation.
The complete product dependency/process boundary admits no mutating Git library or Git subprocess path.
Runtime binding exposes only the user-private Unix-domain endpoint.
The daemon socket and runtime permissions exclude group and other access.
A closed-world daemon source inventory admits no network listener or network I/O API.
The exact daemon dependency graph contains no network client or server dependency.
Unique sentinel bytes are written to a real local artifact and enter the actual hash/attach verification boundary.
Only reference/path, digest, size, and media type persist for the artifact.
The sentinel is absent from every durable request, session, item, job, idempotency, and journal field.
The sentinel remains absent after closing and reopening the real SQLite store.
A mismatching expected Procedure digest rejects before durable admission.
The canonical admitted Procedure snapshot commits atomically with admission and survives reopen.
Exact start replay remains independent of the Procedure source after terminal pruning and Store reopen.
Start idempotency binds the resolved Procedure digest and rejects key reuse with another identity.
Deterministic source deletion, replacement, truncation, symlink, worker-delay, and restart scenarios execute only the admitted snapshot.
Response-loss recovery covers disconnect before and after admission, wait timeout, every job state, domain failure, pruning, missing keys, exact replay, conflicting reuse, and read-only lookup.
